title: After an Almost 20% One-Year Run, is ExxonMobil Still Worth Buying? - The Globe and Mail
content: Exxon MobilCorporationXOM has surged 19.5% over the past year, almost in line with the 19.4% improvement of the composite stocks in the industry. BP plcBP and ChevronCVX, two other integrated players in the same space, have gained 19.6% and 9.7%, respectively, over the same time frame. Since XOM is a large integrated energy giant, investors interested in the stock might have been assessing how the ongoing oil pricing environment is impacting its business fundamentals. Let’s delve deeper into ExxonMobil’s business outlook before concluding on whether to invest in the stock. ExxonMobil has a massive footprint in the Permian, the most prolific oil and gas play in the United States, and offshore Guyana. In the Permian, the integrated giant has been employing lightweight proppant technology and hence is capable of boosting its well recoveries by up to as much as 20%. According to the data from the Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, the shut-in price for existing wells in the Midland, a sub-basin of the Permian, is $42 per barrel. For Delaware, another sub-basin, the Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas estimated the price at $34 per barrel. With West Texas Intermediate (“WTI”) crude oil trading below the $70-per-barrel mark, significantly above the shut-in prices, it makes sense for XOM to continue production in the wells. On the first-quarter earnings call, XOM mentioned that it is on track with its plan of growing its production in the most prolific basin to 1.8 million oil-equivalent barrels this year. Investors should also keep in mind that XOM has a strong balance sheet, on which it could rely during an unfavorable business environment. The debt-to-capitalization of ExxonMobil is 15.4%, which is significantly lower than 29.6% of the industry’s composite stocks. Coming to the integrated energy giant’s dividend commitment story, over the past 43 years, ExxonMobil has been rewarding shareholders with annual dividend hikes at an average rate of 5.8%. Before concluding, we should also consider that WTI crude oil is now significantly down from the more than $100-per-barrel mark reached in May this year. With upstream operations responsible for XOM’s significant earnings generation, softer commodity prices are likely to have hurt the company’s bottom line, as they are affecting both BP and CVX. Also, XOM is currently trading at a premium. The stock is trading at a trailing 12-month EV/EBITDA multiple of 9.06x, which is higher than the broader industry average of 5.49x. BP and CVX, two other integrated majors, are valued at 2.83x and 8.82x, respectively. Thus, investors shouldn’t rush to bet on the overvalued ExxonMobil stock right away. title: This Analyst Just Upgraded Chevron Stock. Here's Why. - inkl
content:
Wolfe Research’s senior analyst Doug Leggate upgraded Chevron (CVX) shares to “Outperform” on July 2, announcing a $210 price target that represents significant upside from current levels. CVX sits a little under its 20-day moving average (MA), with a decisive break above the $178 expected to accelerate bullish momentum in the near term. Chevron stock advanced 1.6% on the day of the upgrade, though it remains well below its 52-week high of nearly $212. The central thesis behind the upgrade rests on a valuation disconnect between what the market is pricing in and CVX stock’s improving fundamentals. Leggate argues that commodity price volatility has obscured genuine improvements in Chevron’s sustainable cash generation capabilities. He contends that the market is currently embedding a long-term Brent oil price assumption below $60 a barrel, which is substantially lower than the normalized forward pricing curve of about $70 per barrel. This gap between implied and expected pricing creates what Leggate views as a compelling entry point for investors willing to look beyond near-term oil market noise. Guyana serves as the most critical near-term growth catalyst in the upgrade thesis. The Uaru development is expected to commence operations and reach a free cash flow inflection point during the second half of 2026, which should bolster Chevron’s financial resilience even in a subdued oil price environment. Over time, Leggate expects Guyana to generate sufficient cash flow to offset dividend obligations tied to the Hess acquisition and eventually become CVX’s “single largest contributor” to free cash flow. The strategic importance of Guyana intensifies as 2033 approaches, when the Tengiz partnership in Kazakhstan reaches its contractual conclusion. Beyond Guyana, Chevron has secured new development opportunities in 2026 across Venezuela, Libya, and Iraq, with a potential ninth Guyana development phase also under consideration. Wolfe Research believes these initiatives could sustain production growth well beyond the end of this decade, providing multi-year visibility into Chevron's growth trajectory. The broader analyst community remains predominantly bullish on CVX shares. The stock carries a consensus “Moderate Buy” rating with a mean price target of $216 across 25 analysts, comprising 19 “Buy,” five “Hold,” and one “Sell” rating. From a technical and valuation standpoint, Chevron Corp is approaching oversold territory with the relative strength index (RSI) currently hovering in the mid-30s. CVX’s most recent quarterly earnings exceeded expectations by $0.41, delivering $1.41 per share versus a $1.00 consensus, and the upcoming Q2 earnings announcement is already being flagged as the next potential catalyst. title: Flutter Entertainment (NASDAQ: FLUT), Lululemon (NASDAQ: LULU), And Chevron (NYSE: CVX): Cash Producers Worth Watching And One To Avoid - foreignpolicyjournal.com
content: By Ewan Scott | Jul 5, 2026 | Economy & Business, Featured, News & Analysis Strong free cash flow is widely regarded as a hallmark of business quality, but high cash generation alone does not guarantee market-beating returns for investors. Some cash-heavy companies struggle with inefficient capital allocation, weakening demand, or deteriorating competitive positioning that erodes long-term value. Flutter Entertainment (NASDAQ: FLUT), the global online sports betting and gaming giant behind FanDuel, PokerStars, Paddy Power, and Sky Betting and Gaming, is one name analysts suggest avoiding despite its scale. Flutter’s trailing 12-month free cash flow margin sits at just 3.7%, a figure that limits its ability to reinvest in growth, repurchase shares, or return meaningful capital to shareholders. The company posted annual revenue growth of 17.8% over the last two years, which fell below the benchmark standard for the consumer discretionary sector given its already large revenue base. Flutter’s subpar operating margin of 2.7% further constrains its capacity to respond to new competitive threats or fund meaningful operational improvements. The stock currently trades at $106.06 per share, implying a forward price-to-earnings ratio of 16.2x, a valuation that appears difficult to justify given the underlying financial profile. On the more favorable side of the ledger, Lululemon (NASDAQ: LULU) stands out as a compelling cash-producing business, carrying a trailing 12-month free cash flow margin of 11.4%. The athletic apparel retailer has demonstrated pricing power and product differentiation that support a best-in-class gross margin of 57.5%, a figure that reflects strong consumer demand for its offerings. Lululemon’s disciplined cost management has produced a two-year average operating margin of 20.8%, and the company continues to aggressively expand its store footprint into new markets. At $118.03 per share and a forward P/E of 10.4x, Lululemon presents a valuation that looks attractive relative to its operational strength and growth trajectory. Chevron (NYSE: CVX), the integrated energy giant with operations spanning deepwater drilling to retail fuel stations, rounds out the watchlist with a trailing 12-month free cash flow margin of 7.3%. Chevron has delivered above-market annual sales growth of 4.1% over the past decade, a notable achievement for a company operating at the scale of $190 billion in annual revenue. That dominant market position provides meaningful fixed-cost leverage as sales expand, allowing the company to generate cash well above what many of its industry peers can achieve. With a 10.4% free cash flow margin exceeding peer averages, Chevron retains considerable flexibility to reinvest in operations or return capital to shareholders through dividends and buybacks. The stock trades at $168.95 per share on a forward P/E of 10x, a valuation that reflects both the cyclical nature of energy markets and the company’s enduring competitive advantages in the sector. He has over two decades of experience in journalism and digital publishing.
